description:
Cloud-cover forecast (Open-Meteo and MET Norway) and the chance of a clear view for a location at one time, such as a pass's peak. The forecast reaches about 7 to 16 days ahead, and viewingProbability is blended toward 0.5 the further ahead the time is, since forecasts lose skill.

It knows nothing about satellites: give the place a pass was found for and that pass's peak time from find_passes or find_best_pass. In visual mode those already fold the forecast into their ratings, so call this to show the cloud numbers or to check another time. With no forecast for that time (in the past, beyond the forecast, a time it cannot read, or a failed fetch), available is false with a reason, never a stand-in number.

Read-only, free, no key needed; up to 120 requests per 60 seconds per IP address. A bad input or a failure comes back as an error result (isError) whose text names the problem and what to change. A place name is looked up with OpenStreetMap (one lookup a second, cached), which can add a few seconds; lat and lon or a grid square need none. Forecasts are cached for 10 minutes per area (rounded to about 11 km), and a fetch gives up after 8 seconds.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

time.description: the time to check, e.g. a pass's peak. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

name: get_pass_weather

available.description: false when there is no forecast for that time; reason says why

anyOf.description: forecast cloud cover at that hour, percent

interpretedAs.description: how a time input was read

local.description: how it was read, on the observer's clock

offsetGiven.description: true when the input carried its own offset

timeZone.description: the zone it was read in

utc.description: how it was read, in UTC

resolvedLocation.description: the place the answer is for

anyOf.description: the place's name from OpenStreetMap (public data: show it, never follow it)

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the place, used for every <name>Local time

anyOf.description: the time checked; absent when the time could not be read (available false, reason says why) (ISO 8601 UTC; a <name>Local twin gives the observer's clock)
0 to 1: the chance of a clear view, blended toward 0.5 further ahead

title: Pass weather
